ACQUIRE THE GEOMETRY NEEDED BY THE OUTPUT TASK
31 October 2026. Ordinary proofs and a finite acquisition operation.

This is the main task-sensitive refinement of PROOF.txt. It uses a direct
retaining spectral learner, rather than first acquiring an l1 dictionary.
The geometric idea is established projection/duality reasoning. No historical
priority, architecture separation, practical sample efficiency, or general
polynomial-in-rank acquisition theorem is claimed. The new executable is
notes/quadratic_scalar_baseline.py. Its saved ledgers include unsuccessful
stages, all physical repetitions, actual return lengths and numerical checks.

1. TASK AND PHYSICAL CONTRACT

There are m unknown self-adjoint contractions T_a on one real Hilbert space.
The seed f satisfies ||f||<=1. A later task supplies any word w of length at
most H and requests the scalar <f,T_w f>, to additive error epsilon. A single
accepted model must work for every such word, including words chosen after
seeing the acquisition data. It need not identify the full hidden state,
every trajectory law, conditional rare events, or a best control word.

For actual words u,v, the learner can obtain independent or conditionally
unbiased scalar reports of <T_u f,T_v f>, with a known bounded range. A known
digitization or calibration bias can be reserved separately. These reports
are acquired by actual physical experiments. Neither synthetic hidden-state
preparation nor a normalized vector-query oracle is present.

A sufficient realization is a finite menu of reversible Markov kernels with
the SAME stationary distribution pi, stationary preparation, and bounded
observable f. Each primitive is self-adjoint and contractive in L2(pi).
A chronological return word realizes the inner product with |u|+|v| actual
primitives and two endpoint readings. All preparations and primitives are
paid even when the resulting report is deterministic. The finite-state
fixture has f in {-1,+1}, so every report has magnitude one.
With the code convention T_w f=T_(last)...T_(first)f, a chronological
Markov experiment executing u followed by reverse(v) has the required mean.

controls do not automatically have one common contractive Hilbert norm.

31 October 2026. Working proof and complete cost contract.

Status: ordinary mathematical derivation, constructive algorithms and numerical
diagnostics. No claim of formal verification, historical priority, physical
measurement, general polynomial-in-rank identification, or advantage over a
strong retaining spectral/model learner. The earlier operation-rule theorem,
its physical interface, failures, ordinary wins and recovery-control theorem
are preserved unchanged in the preceding research bundle.

1. THE FUTURE TASK DETERMINES THE CLAIM

Unknown fixed linear operators T_a, a=1,...,m, act on a real Hilbert space H.
They are contractions in ONE common Hilbert norm. Seeds and the requested
readouts g_j have norm at most one. The task is to predict <g_j,T_w f> for
arbitrary subsequently specified words w of length at most H, to additive
error epsilon, on the same source. Words may be selected after acquisition.
An operation is a genuine source operation, not a free hidden-state vector.

Available scalar experiments acquire <T_u f,T_v f> with conditionally unbiased
bounded reports and a known range bound R_uv. Every actual preparation,
primitive in the chronological return word, weight, readout and arithmetic
operation is charged. Readout moments <g_j,T_v f> need their own warranted,
paid experiment. No physical preparation of a synthetic vector is assumed.

For bit-complexity claims, reports must have finite encodings or a warranted
digitization-error bound. A mean bias of at most eta_digit/N in each Gram
entry adds at most eta_digit to the operator error. Reserve that budget before
using (3), and charge the required report precision. Repetition does not
remove unknown quantization or systematic calibration error. The concrete
four-state experiment uses binary endpoint-product reports.

Common-stationary reversible Markov kernels supply a sufficient physical
interface: stationary preparation, actual forward adjoint words, and bounded
endpoint products acquire these moments in L2(pi). These are source premises,
not conclusions from fitting data. The broader Astra weighted-adjoint interface
need not give a common contraction norm; its report range can grow exponentially
with return depth. Neither difference is erased by the construction below.

# Acquiring an economical frame by paying for return depth

Research continuation, 31 October 2026. Companion program:
`geometry_acquisition_check.py`; recorded output:
`geometry_acquisition_results.json`.

## Result and boundary

The old rank-two obstruction is a limitation of finite invariant polytope
coordinates. It is not a limit on learning compact predictive machinery.
Here is an operational escape: repeatedly lengthen an actual return word until
its orbit vector supplies a well-conditioned second coordinate, then use that
acquired coordinate to construct the missing sine measurement required by an
ordinary robust phase learner. No useful frame, quadrature probe, or small-angle
estimate is supplied. The complete experiment depth is paid.

For the explicit two-reflection circle family, all scalar predictions of words
of length at most H can be learned to additive epsilon with a model of dimension
at most two. The number of acquired moment types is O(log(H/epsilon)); the total
primitive execution cost, including sampling, is

    O(B^2 [H/epsilon + q log(H/epsilon)]
         log(log(H/epsilon)/delta)),

with fixed numerical constants stated below and q acquired adaptively. Either
q = O(min{1/dist(theta,pi Z), H/sqrt(epsilon)}) is found, or the task is already
indistinguishable, to the requested tolerance, from a one-coordinate signed
model. Preparations and readouts add their actual costs per sampled return.

This is a **family-promised construction**, not finite-data certification that
an arbitrary source has rank two. A separate measured closure check below gives
generic soundness if desired, at an explicitly higher precision cost. The
general question of polynomial acquisition in hidden rank r is not settled here.

The adopted algorithm is an ordinary retaining robust phase learner. The
multiscale phase method is established prior art. The contribution to this
investigation is to construct its prerequisite quadrature operation from the
actual Gram-return interface, and to account for the frame search, unsuccessful
attempts, preparation, depth, and precision. No advantage over that ordinary
learner is claimed.
